title: Sparkling Water 12-pack

drivers.name: Promotion: 20% off
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted uplift from 16 past promotions: x1.58; this week’s 20% off is deeper than 10% and 15% off, but similar to 25% off which lifted x1.55 in 2026-07-20. Shrink slightly due to one past occurrence at this depth.

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C)
drivers.evidence: July 2026 promotion during heatwave drove x1.55 vs baseline. Similar heatwave conditions in prior weeks increased sales. No prior heatwave with this magnitude in October, but consistent with summer patterns. Noise-adjusted effect shrunk to 35% uplift.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is deeper than most past promotions (median 16% off), but the 25% off in 2026-07-20 drove x1.55 vs baseline, and the 25% off in 2026-03-16 drove x2.74. The noise-adjusted estimate for promotions is x1.58. The heatwave (38°C) is a strong demand driver, consistent with summer spikes and the 25% off week in July. The baseline already reflects seasonal trend, but the heatwave and promotion are distinct drivers. Halloween is not the same week—last year's week before was a dip, but this is not the event week. No pantry-loading effect expected as this is not the week after a promotion. The classical model underweights the heatwave. Shrink promotion effect slightly due to high price cut and limited past data at this depth. Combine multiplicative; adjust toward baseline due to noise.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 95.5 | 5%-95%: 28.9 - 183.3 | 10%-90%: 61.2 - 151.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-39% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
